summary: Build practical oil and gas production and field operations skills through five days of applied surveillance, safety, optimization, and reporting exercises.
lede: Oil and gas production training equips field professionals to assess well and facility performance and make sound operating decisions. Designed for production engineers, field supervisors, process operators, and maintenance coordinators, it develops skills in interpreting pressure and flow trends, diagnosing production constraints, and using surveillance data to guide operating choices. Learners also practice reviewing safety barriers, prioritizing equipment work, and turning field findings into a production dashboard and action plan.
audienceIntro: This course suits intermediate professionals who already work with field assets, operating data, work control, or production reporting and need a stronger end-to-end view of oil and gas production.
modules: Process Safety and Field Work Control
Production Reporting and Field Action Planning
prerequisites: You should have approximately one year of exposure to oil and gas field operations, production reporting, well surveillance, process operations, maintenance coordination, or HSE activities. You should be comfortable reading basic process flow diagrams, production tables, equipment records, and operating procedures. No programming is required. Advanced analytics, AI-assisted anomaly detection, and Power BI use are taught at operational application level, while production optimization and process safety exercises focus on supervised analysis rather than production-system implementation.
